title: engine/ready
description: Engine-to-shell notification, sent once after the `initialize` answer (brief 0038): the engine's Chrome DevTools remote debugging port answers. The engine chose a free port on 127.0.0.1 before CefInitialize (CEF binds the DevTools HTTP and websocket server to 127.0.0.1 only) and sends this once `GET /json/version` on it answered. A debugger (vscode-js-debug's `pwa-chrome` attach) reaches the engine's tabs there; the shell never guesses the port. Absent when the port did not answer within 10 s (the engine logs why on stderr): the tabs then cannot be debugged, and the shell knows only `initialize`'s `sandbox`. Brief 0039 adds how the engine is sandboxed and which CEF it loaded.

remoteDebuggingPort.description: The remote debugging port (CEF accepts 1024 to 65534).

address.description: Where it listens: always the loopback address.

sandbox.description: How Chromium's sandbox runs (brief 0039, browsers/chromium/README.md): `namespaces`, unprivileged user namespaces (the kernel allows them; the engine probed `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` in a forked child before CEF started); `helper`, the setuid `chrome-sandbox` beside `libcef.so` (owned by root, mode 4755) where namespaces are not available; `none`, `--no-sandbox`, only when the engine's command line carries `--allow-no-sandbox` (the workspace's opt-in or ELUDITE_CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1 in the shell) and neither of the others can work or the engine runs as root.

cefDir.description: The CEF folder the engine loaded its resources and locales from (`--cef-dir`, else `libcef.so`'s folder beside the engine: its own, or `cef/` in a package).
